Definition: a bath or Hebrew measure (as a means of division) of liquids
BiblicalUsage: Bath is a measure for liquids, the bath of the temple's great sea and of the offerings. Solomon's molten sea holds two thousand baths, the law fixes the bath as a tenth of a homer so that measures are honest, and Isaiah says ten acres of vineyard will yield one bath of wine.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God's measures are a sermon on honesty, because He fixes the bath and the ephah so that no man can cheat his neighbour with a false measure. The temple sea holds its thousands of baths by His order, and I hold that a God who measures wine cares about honest dealing in the market too.
